findings.what: The old `.trim_end()` was dropped, so a message ending in a newline (such as a `toml_edit` parse error) now keeps it, `writeln!` prints a blank line, and the existing `a_message_that_ends_in_a_newline_does_not_print_a_blank_line` test breaks; trailing spaces on the last line also reach the stream again.

The diff moves indentation into the emitter but only updates the test fixture, so any caller that still writes `\n  ` (the removed test copied the refusal messages' old `\n  ` convention) will now print its continuation lines with four spaces.
Only a truly empty line skips the indent, so a line holding only spaces (now that nothing trims) gets two more spaces of trailing whitespace, the exact case the doc comment says it avoids.
